Hi Sam — great to hear from you. Appreciate the clear asks; I summarized answers below and attached a short proposal workbook that maps pool sizes to throughput and pricing. (See attachment: redwood-multiregion-pricing-v1.xlsx)

Short answers:
- Separate regional pools: yes — we treat US-West and US-East as distinct Dedicated pools. You can reserve capacity independently (separate commits) or purchase a single cross-region commitment with a defined routing policy.
- Cross-region routing: optional. By default requests route to the local pool; we can enable smart-failover which will automatically route to a sibling pool on capacity shortfall. That adds a small routing surcharge but preserves SLOs.
- Replication/DR: two recommended patterns:
  • Active-active (preferred for low-latency production): each region has pinned model replicas; KV caches are local, and we support async warm-cache replication across regions — fast warmup but not synchronous.
  • Active-standby with synchronous state replication: available for enterprise customers as part of a DR add-on (adds replication overhead and affects throughput guarantees).

I've looped in Dev for the technical trade-offs and Logan for pricing/commit sizes. Marissa is on the thread for approvals on discounts for enterprise pilots.

Next steps I propose:
1) Dev to confirm throughput hit for synchronous replication per pool size.
2) Logan to propose two pricing options: (A) separate commits per region, (B) consolidated cross-region commit with routing add-ons.
3) We’ll produce a short one-page summary for procurement to sign-off.

Hey all — quick technical note on replication and throughput implications. I’m including expected ballpark numbers so procurement can evaluate trade-offs.

Context: baseline is a single region pool with N GPUs (A100/H100 equivalence). For ClearSky we recommended two baseline pool sizes in the workbook (16-GPU and 64-GPU).

Synchronous replication (state + KV):
- Mechanism: write-ack flow requires cross-region replication of KV deltas; this puts additional tail-latency on step writes and reduces effective sustained TPS roughly by ~15–25% depending on inter-region RTT and model prompt length.
- Cost: additional egress and one standby replica (effectively 2x instances for stateful replication).
- When to choose: mission-critical inference where consistency matters (e.g., financial reconciliations).

Async warm-cache / active-active:
- Mechanism: caches replicate asynchronously; on failover we perform fast warmup and route in-flight requests to the healthy region.
- Impact: negligible TPS hit in steady-state. Recovery/initial cold misses will cost tokens but warm quickly.
- Cost: replication bandwidth only; no full 2x replica required.

Throughput guarantees:
- For Dedicated pools with active-active, we guarantee per-pool throughput up to the committed TPS in each region. With cross-region smart-failover enabled, we maintain SLOs but we recommend a 10% headroom on commit to absorb routing surges.

I'll attach a short note to the workbook with the expected TPS deltas per model family (small/medium/large). Happy to run a short pro forma test on your sample prompts if you share a small prompt set (10–20) and target latency.

- Dev
